detailed_description: The JSON to Rust converter generates simple Rust struct definitions from pasted JSON in the browser. You can edit the root struct name, toggle Serde derives, and choose whether null values become Option<serde_json::Value>. The converter parses JSON with JSON.parse, uses the first item of an array when the input is an array of objects, creates nested structs for nested objects, infers basic Rust types such as String, i64, f64, bool, Vec, and serde_json::Value, and adds serde rename attributes when field names are converted to snake_case. The generated code appears in a readonly textarea and can be copied. It does not import JSON files, validate schemas, choose Rust editions, configure visibility, generate enums or From traits, or add documentation comments.
usage_steps: Paste JSON into the input textarea or edit the sample object.
Choose whether to include Serde derives and whether null values should use Option.
Click Convert to generate Rust struct code.
Review the output textarea and copy the generated code when needed.
usage_examples: Generate a starter Rust struct from a small API response sample.
Create nested structs from a pasted object that contains a child object.
Compare output with and without Serde derives before copying the code.
Use the first object in a sample array to scaffold a basic Rust struct.
